Convention Establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA, 1960, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA; SR 955.0; Geldwaeschereigesetz, GwG), as amended; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 697i on the register of beneficial owners; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis and 305ter; FINMA Circular 2020/1 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; Federal Act on Embargoes (Embargo Act, SR 946.231); Handelsregisterverordnung (HRegV; SR 221.411).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially executed and certified Articles of Association (Statuten / status) of the Aktiengesellschaft
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public competent in the canton of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the Articles are to be used abroad; no consular legalization is required for apostille members of the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of a non-resident corporate shareholder or, for individual shareholders, a certified passport copy and proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or national passport authority / notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the origin country is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention, consular legalization by the competent Swiss embassy/consulate is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-wealth and bank reference letter issued by a regulated financial institution for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas or Swiss AML-regulated bank/professional KYC provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the relevant hosting notary/authority where available; otherwise consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the founding shareholders and all beneficial owners holding 25% or more of votes or capital must be screened against: (i) Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions/embargo lists under the Embargo Act; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists as implemented in Swiss law; (iii) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists where USD payment rails are used; and (iv) domestic Swiss politically exposed person (PEP) indicators per AMLA and FINMA Circular 2020/1. Enhanced due diligence and senior compliance approval are mandatory for PEPs or any beneficial owner resident in a high-risk jurisdiction. Re-screening at least annually is recommended and must be documented in the UBO and KYC files.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (zefix.ch); Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC); the actual filing is made through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name of an Aktiengesellschaft must include the legal form suffix 'AG' or the full word 'Aktiengesellschaft' in the relevant local official language (also 'SA' for French/Italian). The name may be selected in any language written in Latin script; non-Latin alphabets require an official transliteration into Latin characters. The name must not be misleading, must not imitate a protected mark, and must comply with public-order and naming rules under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 950 et seq. and Handelsregisterverordnung.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca – requires FINMA banking licence
Versicherung / Insurance / Assicurazioni – requires FINMA insurance authorisation
Eidgenossenschaft / Bund / Confederation – reserved for federal or public-law entities
Swiss National Bank / Banque Nationale Suisse / Schweizerische Nationalbank
Suisse / Schweiz / Swiss – permitted only where the name has a sufficient factual connection and does not imply government affiliation
Trust / Fiduciary – may trigger specific cantonal licensing and register requirements
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation, where granted by a cantonal commercial register office, is valid for 30 calendar days and may be extended in writing before expiry for a further 30 days upon showing good cause. If the name is rejected, the applicant must request a formal written refusal (Verfügung) from the cantonal Commercial Register Office. Within 30 days of service of that refusal, the applicant may appeal to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde). A further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in St. Gallen under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act (VwVG, SR 172.021).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-only address is not acceptable as the registered office. Swiss law requires a physical address in the registered canton where statutory records are kept and official process can be served. A licensed domiciliation/registered-agent arrangement is permissible for ISIC 4620 raw cotton trading, but the service provider must maintain a genuine physical presence and accessible personnel; a pure virtual mailbox does not satisfy commercial-substance expectations for an AG.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low-to-moderate: approximately 10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first three years for a low-risk commodities trading AG. The likelihood increases if the company uses a domiciliation agent without adequate substance, trades with high-risk jurisdictions, or triggers sanctions/embargo alerts.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial fee scale based on capitalization and scope; market benchmark CHF 1,800–3,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) publication and legal advertising fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Zefix)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial setup and first-year maintenance under Art. 697i of the Swiss Code of Obligations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss registered agent / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for domiciliation and UBO compliance services; CHF 800–1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page translator tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service for the first year at a cantonal registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for physical registered office and corporate secretarial services in Geneva, Zug or Zurich; CHF 2,500–5,000 per year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620 to 679 (Aktiengesellschaft / stock company), supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) and the Federal Act on the Commercial Register of 23 September 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton where the registered office is located, under the supervisory coordination of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Federale Dienst für das Handelsregister), with public search access via Zefix
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation together with the Articles of Association (Statuten) filed electronically through the eGRIS platform for entry into the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (including at least CHF 100 per registered share), of which at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) must be fully paid up in cash before registration; the paid-up amount must be deposited into an escrow or blocked account (Sperrkonto) at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank, and the bank's confirmation of deposit is required for filing; release of funds occurs only after conclusive commercial register registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CH AG (DRAFT). The incorporators, acting as provisional administrators, hereby resolve: (1) The Articles of Association as notarized are approved and adopted; (2) The entire share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, is subscribed and fully funded as confirmed by the bank's escrow certificate; (3) The registered office is established at Bahnhofstrasse 12, 8001 Zurich, Switzerland; (4) [Anna Müller] and [Lukas Keller] are appointed as members of the Board of Directors, with Anna Müller as Chairperson; (5) The Board is authorized to execute registration filings, open bank accounts, engage auditors, and obtain all tax and insurance registrations. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and pre-incorporation eligibility check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the Zefix online registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Zefix and Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB) search to confirm the availability of the company name 'CH AG'; verify that the proposed corporate purpose (international brokerage of ginned raw cotton and synthetic yarns) is lawful and not subject to prior approval; confirm that each director and authorised signatory is eligible to act (no adjudication of incapacity or disqualifying criminal record); reserve the exact name for subsequent notarial use
required_dossiers: Identity document (passport or national ID) of each incorporator, director, and authorised signatory
Draft Articles of Association including name, registered office, share capital, and purpose
Zefix/SHAB name search and availability receipt
Declaration of eligibility and non-disqualification for each director (self-declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identity confusion or public interest reasons, amend the proposed name to a distinctive alternative and resubmit the reservation request; if a director is deemed ineligible, replace that director before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (for Zurich: Öffentliche Beurkundung by certified notary of the canton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an in-person or Swiss-consular notarial appointment; present the final Articles of Association; incorporate all resolutions on share subscription, board structure, and statutory auditors into the notarial deed; execute the deed before the notary with valid identity documents; the notary verifies legality of the purpose, capital amount, and compliance with minimum capital payment rules
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten) in German or bilingual German/English
Passport or residence permit of all incorporators and directors
Name reservation confirmation
Written instructions on share classes, board composition, and ordinary vs. special auditor appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies in the articles (e.g., capital breakdown, purpose wording), correct the draft and execute a revised deed; no state penalty arises if the deficiency is cured before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of paid-up share capital and bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS AG, Zürcher Kantonalbank, or similar) holding the blocked capital deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the company's future name; deposit the required minimum of CHF 50,000; provide the bank with the notarized draft deed and identification for beneficial ownership verification; obtain the bank's capital confirmation certificate (Einzahlungsbestätigung) stating that the funds are irrevocably blocked until the Commercial Register registration is complete
required_dossiers: Notarized deed and draft Articles of Association
Bank account opening application and due diligence questionnaire
Passport and beneficial ownership declaration for each subscriber
Escrow/blocked account instruction letter permitting release only upon registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital confirmation is rejected due to incomplete beneficial ownership data, resubmit full source-of-funds documentation to the bank; alternatively, appoint a different FINMA-licensed bank for the escrow deposit without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register filing and registration of the Aktiengesellschaft
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) using the eGRIS electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, Articles of Association, capital confirmation, and board resolutions through eGRIS together with the electronic signatures; pay the registration fee; the cantonal registrar reviews legal compliance and issues a verification order (Zwischenverfügung) if any document requires correction; upon final approval, the company is entered in the Commercial Register and published in the SHAB; obtain the Certified Company Extract (Handelsregisterauszug) as proof of legal personality
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank capital confirmation certificate (Einzahlungsbestätigung)
Board of Directors acceptance declarations and specimen signatures
Identity documents of all directors and authorised signatories
Declaration on the location of the registered office (consent of the landlord if the space is not owned)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a verification order, cure the stated formal defects (e.g., supplementary signed declarations, certified translations, or apostilled documents) and resubmit; if the application is rejected, withdraw and refile after correction; any adverse decision may be appealed to the cantonal superior court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT and withholding tax; cantonal tax authorities for corporate income tax; AHV compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) for old-age and survivors insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration form with the ESTV if annual turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000; register with the cantonal tax administration for profit and capital tax assessments; register with the AHV compensation fund for employer's social contributions and with the relevant accident insurance carrier; complete the duty and customs registration with the Federal Customs Administration (FCA) if exports are made directly instead of via a Swiss trading intermediary
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register Extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Articles of Association and board resolution on registered office
Projected turnover statement for VAT threshold determination
Identification documents of directors and payroll contact person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration forms are queried, correct the postal address, legal form code, or expected turnover figure and resubmit via the relevant cantonal coordination office; for delayed VAT registration, request a retroactive registration waiver under Article 25 VAT Act where turnover has not yet exceeded the threshold.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration occupational, civil defense, and operational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal labor inspectorate (Arbeitsinspektorat), SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund), and the cantonal building/fire authority competent for the office site
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with SUVA for occupational accident and non-occupational accident insurance; verify workplace ergonomics and fire safety compliance for the registered office; since the business is pure international brokerage without warehousing, handling, or manufacturing, no Gewerbebewilligung (cantonal trade license) or industrial operating permit is required; if a third-party warehouse is used for physical cotton bale consolidation, contractually require that warehouse operator to hold the applicable building, fire, and environmental permits and to comply with Swiss goods-handling standards
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract confirming legal formation
Office lease contract or sublease with fire safety documentation
Employer declaration for SUVA insurance coverage
List of employees with dates of hire and occupational functions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the cantonal labor inspectorate identifies deficiencies in workplace safety, adopt the stated corrective measures (e.g., first-aid equipment, emergency exits) and submit a declaration of compliance; for storage at a third-party logistics provider, replace the provider or require contractual guarantees of permits and insurance coverage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure commercial brokerage and export trading of ginned raw cotton bales; the relevant regulatory counterpart for export administration is SECO - State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Export Control Division), and the Federal Customs Administration for customs export formalities, neither of which imposes a periodic operating license for cotton brokerage
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 4620 international brokerage activity; the company's status as a licensed export trader is evidenced solely by the Commercial Register entry and the Swiss export declaration records in the customs transit system (NCTS)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Registration and full EIA not required because the activity comprises trading and brokerage only, with no stationary installation, manufacturing, or emissions-generating processes; if the company later operates a cotton bale sorting or repackaging facility, a preliminary screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV) would apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge; no VOC-emitting operations therefore the threshold of 50 mg C/m3 under the Swiss Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV) is not triggered; waste handling, if any, limited to incidental packaging waste and must follow the Ordinance on Waste Movements (VEVA); cotton bales transiting through third-party logistics must be stored in dry, ventilated conditions preventing mould formation and dust emissions, aligned with FOEN guidance on odour and particulate nuisance avoidance

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is handled by the cantonal building insurance authority (Gebäudeversicherung) under VKF/AEAI fire protection regulations requiring smoke detectors, extinguishers, and unobstructed escape routes at the registered office; structural load inspection is applicable only for warehouse use and must be confirmed by the cantonal building inspectorate if the company leases dedicated storage space; occupational workplace clearance comprises SUVA accident prevention inspection covering office ergonomics, first-aid provisions, electrical safety, and employee instruction, together with the employer obligation to register all staff for occupational accident insurance

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration ESTV/AFC (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, Administration fédérale des contributions); official portal: www.estv.admin.ch and taxpayer portal: www.estv.admin.ch/kundenportal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Aktiengesellschaft is first entered in the Commercial Register, which automatically issues the Swiss Federal Statistical Office operating company number UID/IDE/IDI; the UID also serves as the VAT identification number for Swiss VAT purposes. For indirect tax registration, the AG must submit the VAT registration application to the Federal Tax Administration through the E-Services VAT portal, stating the commencement date of taxable activity in Switzerland. A foreign entity without a Swiss registered office or permanent establishment that becomes liable for Swiss VAT must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative and file a special registration form with the ESTV VAT division. The VAT registration certificate is issued after validation of the UID and business address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; AG is a separate legal taxpayer, subject to full unlimited tax liability on worldwide income for Swiss tax purposes, with deviations for foreign permanent establishments and foreign land; shareholders are taxed separately on distributions; no pass-through treatment is available for AG entities
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Swiss law; an AG cannot elect pass-through taxation. Available statutory elections include: (i) Swiss group taxation election under the federal Tax Harmonization Act permitting domestic and foreign group companies to be taxed as a single tax unit, (ii) voluntary Swiss VAT registration for small businesses below the CHF 100,000 threshold, and (iii) VAT aggregation of related Swiss entities during a five-year binding period. Hybrid mismatch rules apply in accordance with the Swiss implementation of the EU anti-tax-avoidance directive; there is no elective disclosure regime for hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT; Mehrwertsteuer, Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual global turnover from taxable supplies (excluding Swiss VAT and after deducting items excluded from taxable consideration) received or accrued during a business year; voluntary VAT registration is permitted below this threshold. A reduced threshold regime exists for persons whose only sufficient taxable activities are covered services or goods under the reverse-charge rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a national real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API stamping, or a pre-clearance electronic invoice system. VAT administration is self-assessment: taxpayers issue invoices without government pre-authorization. However, invoices must contain statutory particulars, including supplier and recipient UID, type of supply, tax rate, amount of tax, and the date of supply. Electronic invoices are accepted, including PEPPOL and Swiss QR-invoice formats, provided the integrity and legibility of the VAT invoice metadata are preserved for the statutory retention period. Software-based cash register systems must comply with the Federal Act on VAT fiscalization requirements, but there is no central government stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate if the goods are physically removed from Swiss customs territory and delivered to a foreign destination; the supplier must obtain the customs export declaration and transport evidence proving that the goods left Switzerland within 30 days of the supply. For services, zero rating applies primarily where the place of supply is outside Switzerland, in particular B2B services to non-resident recipients, transport services related to exported goods, and ancillary services to eligible export transactions; all outward supplies must be supported by contracts, correspondence, and custodian or banking records proving the cross-border nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) and official export certificate
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR road transport waybill
Proof of export payment or Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Federal Tax Administration routinely audits export zero-rating claims and requires the complete retention of all export documentation for at least ten years. If documentary proof of export is missing, insufficient, or contradicted, the VAT deemed exempt must be retroactively reclaimed at the standard rate, together with default interest (currently 3.5% per annum). Intentional falsification or presentation of forged export evidence constitutes tax evasion under the Swiss VAT Act, punishable with a fine of up to CHF 250,000 or imprisonment for serious cases involving fraud, and the VAT debt may be collected from the recipient if the supplier is insolvent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB – Schweizerische Nationalbank; Banque nationale suisse; Banca nazionale svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc with no exchange-control regime on current-account or capital-account transactions. There are no restrictions on inward or outward transfers, dividend remittance, capital repayment, intercompany financing, or forward hedging. Practical hurdles are limited to bank counterparty due diligence under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, sanctions screening, and the 35% Swiss withholding tax on qualifying dividend distributions unless reduced under a tax treaty or relieved via notification procedure. Profit remittance via dividends or branch repatriation is freely permitted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no statutory conversion ratio. Export proceeds may be retained in the currency of receipt, used directly to settle import payables, or converted freely. Statistical reporting obligations apply under the SNB Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Ordinance: resident non-bank enterprises with either consolidated assets above CHF 1 million or annual foreign receipts/payments above CHF 1 million must report cross-border payments and receivables/payables to the Swiss National Bank on a monthly or quarterly basis through the SNB's electronic reporting portal. The reports are for statistics and balance-of-payments compilation, not exchange-control authorisation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury or clearing rail; MEDIUM as a supplementary convenience for small-volume AP/AR payments. Legal constraints: under the Swiss Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FMIA), Financial Institutions Act (FinIA), and Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), only FINMA-licensed or authorised payment institutions and e-money issuers may provide payment services to Swiss-domiciled clients. An offshore digital EMI holding an account in a third country is not a substitute for a Swiss-based transaction account and may create unlicensed payment-service exposure, weak audit evidence, and counterparty risk. A Swiss or FINMA-passported fintech (e.g., Swissquote or licensed neobank) may be acceptable for low-volume disbursements, but corporate raw-cotton trade flows requiring documentary letters of credit, guarantees, and interbank clearing must be executed through a systemically relevant commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for at least one authorised signatory or director of a newly formed Swiss AG, particularly when the beneficial owner resides outside Switzerland or the EEA. Remote opening is possible only where all directors and beneficial owners are resident in low-risk jurisdictions, the corporate structure is transparent, and FINMA-compliant video-identification (notarised copy of the physical ID and live liveness check) is completed. For non-EEA controllers, PEPs, trust structures, or higher-risk trade flows, Swiss banks mandate a physical interview either in Switzerland or at a Swiss consulate, or require an independent Swiss-regulated attorney, fiduciary, or auditor to certify the identity and authority of the signatories. Even where remote opening is allowed, the bank will initially impose lower transaction limits and enhanced post-account-opening monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque UBO chain involving offshore trusts, foundations, or multiple intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organigramme showing legal and economic ownership through Swiss commercial register extracts; notarised declaration of beneficial ownership on the bank's UBO form; certified copies of trust deeds or foundation charters; audited financial statements for material intermediate entities; evidence of economic substance (staff, premises, assets) for each entity in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Raw cotton shipments from or to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, or transit through embargoed ports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificates from competent agriculture or export authorities; full shipping evidence (bills of lading, warehouse receipts, ginnery weighbridge tickets); commercial invoices cross-referenced to independent price benchmarks (Cotlook A or New York cotton futures); irrevocable documentary L/C confirmation; ocean carrier and logistics provider receipts; denial or export-license verification from the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between high turnover, low capitalisation, and expected commodity margins (trade-based money-laundering red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed feasibility study and six-quarter cash-flow projection; audited opening balance sheet or financial statements certified by a Swiss-chartered auditor; signed purchase and sales contracts with bank-verified counterparties; evidence of warehouse and transport capacity; provisional tax returns and VAT registrations demonstrating commercial transparency; track record of similar completed transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment instructions naming third-party beneficiaries, shell intermediaries, or non-documented buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed written instruction with board resolution authorising third-party disbursement or intermediary commission; commercial contracts identifying the intermediary, commission basis, and payment terms; AML screening results for all parties in the payment chain; confirmation from the Swiss receiving bank of the intermediary's own KYC and regulated status; explanations of any split payments or pre-payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholders or beneficial owners flagged as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or having prior financial-judgment history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declaration with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; independent references from a Swiss-regulated fiduciary or auditor; bank certificate confirming no adverse historical defaults; explanation of the commercial rationale for the cotton export business; consent to enhanced monitoring, periodic renewal of KYC, and near-real-time transaction screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for EUR) to the Swiss AG's CHF or foreign-currency account held with a FINMA-licensed bank. The remittance information must state 'Share Capital AG / Commercial Register UID' and, if the bank's system requires an ISO 20022 purpose code, use 'EQUI' (equity) or 'CFIN' (corporate finance). No SNB exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving bank must perform AMLA source-of-funds checks. Supporting documentation must include a board or shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, notarised subscription statements or a share-subscription agreement, a bank confirmation that the capital amount is at the free disposal of the company (as required for commercial-register registration of an AG), and the company's commercial register extract. For capital above CHF 1 million or any non-cash contribution, the bank and a licensed audit firm will require a sworn statement by the auditor and evidence that the amount was actually credited to an escrow or blocked account in the company's name.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for raw cotton exports will use SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments and documentary collection remittances, and a documentary commercial letter of credit (L/C) opened via SWIFT MT700/MT707, with settlement cover transmitted by MT103/MT202. For the CHF-domestic leg, clearing is via SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) operated by SIX Interbank Clearing; EUR legs via TARGET2/SEPA; USD via Fedwire/CHIPS through bank nostro accounts. All payment messages must quote the invoice number, bill of lading number, country-of-origin certificate reference, and Swiss UID; banks run each message through sanctions and prohibition filters. For an L/C, the exporter must present a clean-on-board bill of lading, signed commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, cotton classification certificate (grade, staple, micronaire), weight certificate, and a phytosanitary certificate where required; all documents must be strictly compliant with UCP600. Documentary collections are processed under URC522, with the presenting bank remitting proceeds only against acceptance or payment. Where open-account terms are used, credit risk may be covered by Swiss Export Risk Insurance (SERV) or private credit insurance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards traded under a bank-approved ISDA 2002 Master Agreement / FX CSA, with maturities of up to 24 months, used to lock conversion rates on forecast export receivables or import payables in USD, EUR, CNY, INR, PKR, and other major currencies.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted currencies (Chinese yuan offshore CNH or onshore CNY, Indian rupee, Pakistani rupee, Nigerian naira, Ethiopian birr) with cash settlement in CHF or USD against an agreed fix, to hedge trade receivables or payables without requiring physical settlement in the restricted currency.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS / long-form FX swaps) matching the currency denomination of trade-finance facilities, ECAs, or working-capital debt, executed under standard ISDA/CSA documentation with a FINMA-authorised bank or broker-dealer.

Tom-next and spot conversion transactions for operational treasury purposes, expressly excluded from speculative dealing and governed by an internal treasury policy with pre-trade counterparty limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return (combined Federal, Cantonal and Communal profit and capital tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered office (for the combined federal/cantonal/communal tax return); Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for the federal part on the same form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within the statutory deadline set by the canton, generally within 6 months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year taxpayer commonly no later than 30 June of the following year, with extension available upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at approximately 3.5% per annum, late-payment surcharge, administrative fines up to 30% of the assessed tax in cases of negligence, summary penalty for omission, and potential criminal tax proceedings for wilful evasion; prolonged non-filing may lead to official estimated assessment and seizure proceeding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT (Swiss Goods and Services Tax) return on annual tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV - Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the expiration of the annual tax period (calendar-year taxpayers: by 1 March of the following year); quarterly filers must file by the 60th day after each quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5%-5% on late-settled tax (current rate set by ESTV), late-filing penalty up to USD 5,000 (or higher depending on tax at stake), and for repeated violations an administrative fine up to USD 50,000; input VAT recovery is suspended until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of financial statements, proposal for profit appropriation, and signed minutes (retained in corporate register) - not filed with government but required for corporate secretarial compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders / Board of Directors (the record is kept at the registered office; it must be made available to tax authorities, regulators and the designated auditor upon request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 6 months of the balance-sheet date (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 699); for companies with annual accounts ending 31 December, no later than 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct regulatory filing penalty; failure to convene the AGM within the statutory period is a breach of the board's statutory duties, may render shareholder resolutions contested, and can expose directors to civil liability for damages and to penal sanctions in the event of insolvency or bankruptcy.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is mandatory where, for two consecutive years, the company exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total CHF 20 million (approx. USD 22.5m), annual revenue CHF 40 million (approx. USD 45m), or 250 full-time employees on average. A limited (simplified) audit is required where any two of the following burdens are exceeded: CHF 10m balance sheet, CHF 20m annual revenue, 50 FTE employees. Companies that exceed neither the ordinary nor the simplified audit thresholds may validly opt out of an audit by unanimous shareholder resolution, provided they employ fewer than 10 full-time employees on average and no statutory exception applies. Shareholders representing the majority of capital may nevertheless request an ordinary audit for a limited purpose.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b) as part of the Swiss Code of Obligations; accounting in Swiss Francs in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. For listed and specifically regulated entities, compliance with Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS is required. The statutory ledger includes the balance sheet, income statement, and notes if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No central annual UBO filing exists in Switzerland. The company's obligation is to record every shareholder in the share register and, for bearer shares, the natural person rated as beneficial owner. When shareholding is transferred, a written notification is to be filed with the board of directors, which must update the share register accordingly. The board is required to provide the published identification data to the applicable federal or cantonal supervisory authority upon request. For Swiss tax purposes, annual tax declaration includes a schedule of shareholders holding more than 5% and changes in ownership; this is part of the annual return. The auditor (if appointed) validates the share register and UBO data in the course of the annual audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Board of Directors minutes)
Minute Book of Annual General Meetings and Board Meetings
Register of Bearer Shares (where bearer shares are issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 5,500 per year for a fiduciary/registered office service in a Swiss canton
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 9,000 for an ordinary audit of a mid-sized AG; USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 for a limited review (if not opted out)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct tax on after-tax profit, equivalent to 7.83% pre-tax; combined federal, cantonal and communal rate for a Zug trading AG approximately 14.6%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (holding ≥10% or market value ≥CHF 1m); tax-free distribution of qualifying capital contribution reserves; Zug notional interest deduction on excess equity; cantonal IP/patent box regimes (Geneva, Bern, Zurich); R&D super-deduction in select cantons; group relief unavailable, but group transfer of reserves possible under specific rulings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Zug Cantonal Corporate Tax Return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen Kanton Zug) combined with Direct Federal Tax declaration; e-filing via V-STAR portal of Zug Tax Administration and ESTV online services; VAT returns separately via Swiss Federal Tax Administration eService portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after fiscal year-end; extension to 12 months available on written request; assessment generally completed within 2–3 years of fiscal year-end for audited entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All assets and liabilities as at fiscal year-end in CHF; bank balances, trade receivables, intercompany payables, inventory of cotton bales if held as principal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Swiss and foreign assets in CHF; disclose all foreign bank accounts regardless of residence; no book-tax conformity adjustment required; include accounts of the Swiss permanent establishment only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross commission income from raw cotton brokerage, cost of sales, operating expenses, financial result, net profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare worldwide income attributable to the Swiss AG; recognise commission on delivery/accrual basis; attach margin analysis for ISIC 4620 trade flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income, capital gains and schedule of qualifying participations with holding percentages and acquisition costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate participation exemption with documentary evidence of 10% threshold or CHF 1m market value; attach foreign tax credit computations for dividend taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustment schedule adding back non-deductible expenses: taxes, fines, private expenses, non-market intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain arm's length transfer pricing documentation for management fees, commission sharing and financing costs; disclose advance rulings or TP study references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends, interest and liquidation proceeds subject to 35% Swiss advance withholding tax; remittance summary to ESTV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 103 and payment slips; confirm whether distributions qualify as capital contribution repayment; provide beneficial ownership declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, legal and free reserves, retained earnings; basis for cantonal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zug capital tax approx. 0.04–0.05% of taxable equity; for non-resident-owned AG, only equity allocable to Swiss PE is taxable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax or CHF 1,000–10,000; procedural default fine up to CHF 10,000; negligent tax evasion surcharge 25–100% of evaded tax; qualified tax fraud fine up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; late payment interest at 4.5% p.a.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal advance tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on Swiss-source dividends, refundable or reduced under applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must file Form 82 refund claim or submit Form 823 for reduced-rate at source with ESTV; attach valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; claim within 3 years after the calendar year of distribution; Swiss AG must verify beneficial ownership and economic substance in Switzerland to prevent treaty abuse under MLI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Swiss WHT; interest on listed or Swiss bank obligations: 35% statutory WHT unless DTA reduction (treaty rates typically 0–10%); arm's length trade debt interest on documentary Letters of Credit and ordinary supplier payables is exempt; cotton brokerage commission income is not subject to Swiss WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No codified CHF threshold for Local/Master File; CbCR mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ CHF 900m; prudent threshold for temporary Swiss TP documentation is related-party transactions ≥ CHF 1m annually or intercompany financing ≥ CHF 500,000; ESTV may request OECD-aligned TP documentation on audit regardless of de minimis levels.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) do not apply directly; however, OECD/MLI and Art. 210 DBG anti-abuse rules require effective substance for treaty benefits, participation exemption and PE attribution: own physical office, resident managing director, local accounting and strategic decision-making in Switzerland; Zug trading AG should employ operational staff for brokerage if annual commission income exceeds CHF 5m; artificial interposition without substance is retroactively recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or false declaration of cotton brokerage commissions; fabricated supplier invoices or side agreements inflating costs; concealment of foreign bank accounts or receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of 1–3× the evaded tax plus penalty interest at 4.5% p.a.; criminal fine up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; publication of judgment; asset seizure under Art. 70–72 Swiss Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for restitution under Art. 754 CO; travel bans and exit restrictions; extradition within EFTA/EU frameworks; disqualification from Swiss board offices up to 5 years; personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividend or quasi-dividend shareholder loan without collecting and remitting 35% withholding tax; reclassifying dividend as untaxed capital repayment without prior ruling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AG liable for 35% WHT plus 5% late-remittance interest and penalty surcharge up to 100% of unremitted amount; ESTV enforcement via bank account attachment and bankruptcy proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally solidarily liable where WHT was collected or utilizable but not remitted; criminal liability for debt fraud under Art. 166 Criminal Code; personal bankruptcy initiated by ESTV.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registered AG without real office, employees, local management or decision-making; interposed solely to hold cotton trading book and obtain treaty relief for foreign beneficiaries; nominee directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and retroactive taxation of undistributed profits with penalty interest; denial of participation exemption and DTA benefits; dissolution proceedings; fines up to CHF 30,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners subject to governance liability under Art. 754 CO; international judicial assistance and travel bans; personal tax assessments in residence country under AEOI data exchange; restitution orders with personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoiced raw cotton bales routed through intermediary jurisdictions for hidden profit repatriation; false customs declarations; circular payments through private accounts; failure to verify beneficial ownership under due diligence obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative AML fines up to CHF 500,000; criminal money laundering penalties under Art. 305bis/305ter Swiss Criminal Code with imprisonment up to 3–5 years; confiscation of instrumentalities and proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorised signatories exposed to negligence-based liability under Swiss AML Act; travel bans and passport seizure; cross-border cooperation under CARF/AEOI exposing personal and corporate accounts; disqualification from financial intermediation.
